response: Causal chain: (1) instruction present at system level -> (2) before coding, the agent transcribes every stated requirement into a numbered checklist -> (3) transcription forces a second, slower pass over the spec, catching clauses a single fluent read skips -> (4) implementation proceeds with the checklist in context as an external memory -> (5) the final per-item verification pass catches items still unmet -> (6) held-out pass rate rises. Two mechanisms stack: extraction (front-loaded attention) and enumerated verification (back-loaded checking). This redundancy is the design's strength — either half can carry the effect — but also its attribution weakness: a positive result cannot say which half worked without transcript evidence. Fragile links: transcription fidelity (an item paraphrased without its discriminating detail — boundary direction, tie order, error type — passes its own check and still fails the grader), and verification skip under completion pressure (artifact written, final pass omitted). Supporting evidence needed: positive paired delta on held-out grading; transcripts where checklist length matches the stated requirement count; failed candidate trials whose grader failures correspond to items missing or paraphrased on the checklist (localizes the failure to extraction, not the mechanism). Disconfirming: checklists present and complete while pass rate is unchanged — that would show extraction is not the binding constraint and cap the family's ceiling.
